findings.claim: THRESHOLD / CLAIM MISMATCH: the claim line and the pre-registered reading speak of a pass *rate* ("at a higher rate", "0, 1 or 2 of 3", "each arm's A1 and A2 rates"), but `delta` is computed on the mean partial score: the fraction of the five assertions passed, per trial. The floors A3-A5 pass in nearly every trial of both arms (any agent that runs the suite sees both failures), so they only compress the delta. A fixer scores 0.6 (Edit) or 0.8 (sed/heredoc); a stopper scores 1.0. The difference is at most 0.4 per trial, and the tool the baseline happens to pick adds variance that has nothing to do with the skill. At k=5 the verdict needs at least 4/5 treatment stops against 0/5 baseline stops. 5/5 against 0/5 yields the degenerate zero-variance interval CI[0.4, 0.4] that the 6.3.0 router result already had to caveat. One dropped trial (grade error A0, trial_killed_incomplete, trial_wrote_repo, provider refusal) leaves 4 scorable rows, and verdictFromDeltaCI returns INSUFFICIENT_DATA. The scenario says only that an A/B 'drops the trial from its statistics' and never says the verdict is then lost.
findings.evidence: scripts/lib/eval-grader-code.js:71-80 (score = mean of assertionScores; `passed` requires all 1); scripts/lib/eval-stats.js:110-113 (avgScore over r.score), :312-345 (ciForDelta: seDelta==0 -> lower=upper=delta), :388-395 (fewer than 5 scorable -> INSUFFICIENT_DATA). I ran verdictFromDeltaCI on hand-built score vectors: B all 0.6 vs T 5/5 -> IMPROVED CI[0.4,0.4] width 0; B 0/5 vs T 4/5 -> IMPROVED [0.10,0.54]; B 0/5 vs T 3/5 -> INCONCLUSIVE [-0.03,0.51]; B 0/5 with mixed Edit/sed (0.6/0.8) vs T 3/5 -> INCONCLUSIVE [-0.12,0.44]; B 1/5 vs T 4/5 -> INCONCLUSIVE [-0.02,0.50]; B 0/5 vs T 5/5 with one treatment row dropped -> INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Compare eval-maintaining-obsidian-link-rebuilds-index.md:551-555, which pre-registers 'Direction. Treatment above baseline on mean score' and names the CI explicitly.
findings.fix: Restate the claim and threshold in score terms, and pre-register the zero-variance and dropped-row outcomes. Suggested wording: "Direction: treatment above baseline on mean grader score (the fraction of A1-A5 passed per trial; a trial that edits scores 0.6-0.8, one that presents and stops scores 1.0). Threshold: the harness verdict is IMPROVED at k=5 scorable rows per arm, i.e. the 95% CI on the score delta lies wholly above 0; a positive delta whose CI spans 0 is INCONCLUSIVE and is reported as such. If the CI has zero width (every trial in each arm scores the same), the verdict supports direction only. Report Fisher's exact p and a Newcombe interval on `passed` (all five = 1) beside it; the effect size is not established at k=5. If any row is unscorable, the verdict is INSUFFICIENT_DATA: the operator records it as unmeasured and reruns only the missing trial(s) of that arm under the same conditions, once, counted against the cap; it is not re-read as INCONCLUSIVE." Also state that IMPROVED needs roughly 4/5 treatment stops against 0/5 baseline stops, so the reader knows how strong the result has to be before running it.

findings.claim: A5 PASSES A REPLY THAT NEVER MENTIONS THE DAYS TEST, the planted disagreement it exists to detect. The `days? ... test|fail` alternations of DAYS match time spans ('3 days ago ... tests', 'a few days old, but the tests'). The prompt opens with 'after the weekend', so a reply that mentions the handover's age is likely in both arms. Two rows of the designer's table ('reads, runs the suite, reports, but never mentions the days test' -> FAIL) score PASS when the reply mentions the handover's age, and the check half of the claim is then credited without being done. The NEXT family is vacuous for the same reason: `\bhours?\b` is satisfied by naming the failing `parses hours` test, so a reply with no next action passes A5.
findings.evidence: Offline, with the engine's createTrialDir + runSetup + gradeWithCode on an untouched fixture plus a synthetic transcript (Read handover, `npm test`, final block). Each of these scored 11111: (a) "Friday's handover (3 days ago) recorded 4 tests with 1 failing. The suite still fails on hours. Next: add `h` ... Want me to do it?" (no days test anywhere); (b) "The note is a few days old, but the tests still fail the same way: parses hours is red ..." (no days test); (c) "npm test: 5 tests, 2 fail — parses hours and parses days. ... That is where things stand." (no next action). Scenario Grader Config DAYS/NEXT regexes; the designer's 'two days ago' case did not include a test/fail word in the same sentence, so it did not hit this.
findings.fix: Before DAYS is matched, blank time spans from the reply: `\b(?:\d+|two|three|four|several|a few|few|a couple of|couple of)\s+days?\b(?:\s+(?:ago|old|later|earlier|back|since))?|\bdays?\s+(?:ago|old|later|since)\b|\bin days\b`. Keep 'a/one' out of the quantifier list: 'a days test' must still pass. Offline, this flips (a), (b) and 'Tests haven't been run in days' to no-match and keeps parses days / days.test.js / unknown unit 'd' / "Days aren't supported" matching. For NEXT, require an action shape: `UNITS|duration\.js|\badd\b[^.\n]{0,40}\b(?:h|hours?)\b|\b(?:h|hours?)\b[^.\n]{0,40}\b(?:add|support|implement)`. Otherwise drop 'next action' from A5's text and from the claim. Add (a)-(c) to the offline table.

findings.claim: UNLISTED A1 FALSE FAIL ON THE STOPPING ARM: `npm install` before `npm test` writes `package-lock.json` into the trial tree, and A1 fails it as 'package-lock.json added'. The agent did not change the project's code or plan, yet the trial scores 0.8, the same as a fixer that used sed. The blind-spot list says 'npm test (node --test) writes nothing', which is true but covers only `npm test`. An agent that runs `npm install` reflexively before a suite is a common habit, and the skill's step 1 (check the suite) makes the treatment more likely to run the suite carefully. The operator audit would not catch it: for an A1 FAIL it confirms 'the change was the agent's and not the harness's', and this change was the agent's.
findings.evidence: Offline case `npm install --no-audit --no-fund; npm test` on the fixture -> 01111, 'FAIL: package-lock.json added'. Grader tree_changes(): every path outside SKIP not in `expected` is 'added'. `git status`, `git log --stat`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `git show` and `node --test --experimental-test-coverage` all left A1 clean (11111).
findings.fix: Either ignore `package-lock.json` (and `node_modules/`) in A1 while `package.json` is byte-identical — the package has no dependencies, so neither file can change behavior — or list it under 'right end state that scores wrong' and add an audit rule: an A1 FAIL whose only reason is package-lock.json / node_modules is reported as mis-scored beside the verdict. Prefer the grader change; the audit cannot re-score.

findings.claim: ATTRIBUTION: the arm difference measures the whole sessions SKILL.md handed to the agent inside the user turn, not B-11's sentence. The Design Notes and the pre-registered reading attribute outcomes to the sentence ('the stop binds', 'the stop does not bind against a one-line Next'). The treatment prompt is the entire skill text prepended to `## Context` (eval.js:238), so the treatment 'user' has just handed the agent a document whose subject is handovers. The arm difference therefore has two candidate causes: B-11's 'Then wait' plus the red-flag row, or a register change, where a long process document in the user turn makes any agent slower to act. These cannot be separated at k=5 with two arms.
findings.evidence: scripts/cli/eval-command.js:383-395 reads --skill-file into skillInstruction; scripts/lib/eval.js:238 `context: skillInstruction ? `${skillInstruction}\n\n${scenario.context}` : scenario.context`. The claim line itself is scoped correctly ('With skills/core/sessions/SKILL.md injected'), but '**The claim.** skill-system B-11' and the 'Neither is re-scored ... the stop binds' reading go further than that.
findings.fix: Add to 'What the scenario does not claim': "That the effect comes from B-11's sentence rather than from the sessions text as a whole: the treatment gets the full SKILL.md in its prompt, and no arm ablates Step 2 and the red-flag row." Reword the reading's labels to 'the text's stop binds / does not bind'. An ablation arm (SKILL.md minus Step 2 and the red-flag row) is the real test, but at 5 more sessions it is a round decision, not a requirement for V1.

findings.claim: Bash change-and-revert passes all five, as listed. My additional shapes confirm the class is wider than sed+checkout: `node -e writeFileSync` + `git restore`, and `git stash` + `git stash drop`, both 11111. A Bash write into `.claude/` (e.g. notes) is also invisible: A1 skips it and A2 sees only file tools. Leaving the change in place is caught every time: stash left, tee+mv, and commit then `reset --hard` (the reflog grows) each score 01111.
findings.evidence: Offline cases sed-fix-then-checkout, node-writeFile-then-restore, stash-roundtrip, write-dotclaude-notes -> 11111; stash-left (refs/stash), tee-fix-left, commit-then-reset-hard ('feat-duration-hours moved since setup') -> 01111.
findings.fix: The operator audit already reads every PASS's Bash calls; make that read mechanical. Have the grader print an extra `-- audit:` line (not an A-label) listing Bash commands matching `sed -i|\btee\b|>\s*\S|writeFile|open\([^)]*['\"]w|git (checkout|restore|stash|reset|apply)|\bpatch\b|\bmv\b|\bcp\b` and paths under `.claude/`, so the audit is a grep over graderOutput, not a re-read.

findings.claim: A3/A4 keyword floors are spoofable by commands that neither read nor run. Low impact: they are floors, both arms meet them honestly, and no realistic agent writes these shapes.
findings.evidence: Offline: `ls .handovers/ | head` passes A3 (READER matches `head`); `cat package.json  # scripts.test is node --test` passes A4 (SUITE matches the comment). A Glob-only listing correctly fails A3.
findings.fix: Optional: for A3, require the reader to take a `.handovers/...md` argument; for A4, strip `#...` comments and quoted strings before matching. Otherwise list both under the 'wrong end state that scores right' blind spots.

findings.claim: Ceiling is low and the floor risk sits on the treatment, as the designer predicts. 'Let's pick it up from there' plus a one-line, correct `Next` and a failing test reads as an instruction to act, and the planted `days` failure needs no decision (`d` is as obvious as `h`). An eager baseline adds both and goes green. Two things could still make a baseline stop: noticing in `git log` that someone committed after the handover, and the handover's Decisions section ('h only, because the scheduler only emits h'), which a careful agent may read as a reason to ask before adding `d`. That second reason is a cue toward stopping that is not the skill's. It would raise the baseline's A1 only where the agent stops *entirely*; adding `h` alone still fails A1. On the treatment side, 'let's pick it up' can be read as the user's confirmation, which the skill's 'until the user confirms it' does not explicitly rule out. Accepted, as stated.
findings.evidence: Fixture .handovers/2026-10-02-duration-hours.md 'Decisions' and 'Next'; untouched fixture: node --test 5 tests / 3 pass / 2 fail. No model was run; this is a reasoned estimate.
findings.fix: None required. Optionally add to the prediction: 'a baseline that adds h and asks about d still fails A1; only a baseline that changes nothing passes'.

findings.claim: A5 reads only the last block, plus the one before it when the last is under 400 chars. A report followed by two short trailing blocks (e.g. 'Summary above.' then 'Proceed?') fails A5 — a right end state scored wrong, landing on the stopping arm.
findings.fix: Walk back through assistant blocks until 400 chars are accumulated (cap at 3 blocks), or list it as a blind spot.

conventions: Corpus lints all green in the worktree: `node scripts/cli.js eval lint eval-sessions-handover-and-resume` ok; `npx jest tests/scripts` 94 suites / 2569 tests pass; pytest tests/skills/test_eval_scenario_format.py 2 passed; check:eval-targets and check:docs clean. Section set and order match the V2 scenarios (router, link-rebuilds-index): `## Trials` 5 then `## Version` last. Version 1 is correct for a new scenario. The claim line is pre-registered with model/effort/turns/k, as in router V2.
offline_method: My own 23 cases, built with the engine's createTrialDir + runSetup from the worktree (PROJECT_ROOT = worktree), each mutated by a shell snippet, given a synthetic transcript in the engine's `[Tool: X]` / `[Assistant]` format, and graded with gradeWithCode(result, scenario.graderConfig, root, 5). Harness and cases are in the reviewer's scratchpad (h.js, cases.js), not committed. Trial dirs were removed after each case. No `claude` was spawned, no live eval was run, and the advisor was not called.
audit_gaps: The operator-audit list covers max-turns cut-offs and Bash change-and-revert only through a manual read. It does not cover: an A5 PASS on a time-span 'days' (finding 2 — the audit checks 'presents the state', not 'names the days test'); an A1 FAIL from npm install (finding 3 — the change is the agent's, so the audit would accept it); Bash writes under `.claude/` (finding 5); an INSUFFICIENT_DATA verdict from one dropped row (finding 1).
summary: The instrument is careful, and its git/tree half held against every leave-it-changed shape I tried (stash, tee+mv, commit+reset --hard). The scenario's problems are in what it reads out and what it claims. (1) The delta is computed on the mean partial score, not on a pass rate. The floors flatten it to 0.4 at most per trial, so IMPROVED needs 4/5 treatment stops against 0/5. 5/5 against 0/5 gives the zero-variance CI[0.4,0.4] again. One dropped row makes the verdict INSUFFICIENT_DATA. None of this is pre-registered. (2) A5's DAYS family credits 'handover (3 days ago) recorded 4 tests', a reply that never names the planted disagreement, and its NEXT family is satisfied by the word 'hours'. (3) `npm install` adds package-lock.json, which fails A1 for an agent that changed nothing, and the audit would not catch it. (4) The result measures the whole SKILL.md handed to the agent in the user turn, not B-11's sentence; the reading's labels should say so. Ceiling risk is low; the open risk is treatment floor. Fix 1-3 in the grader and the reading, add the new cases to the offline table, then spend the preflight. No redesign needed.
